# Founding ML Engineer — Live Music Intelligence

Gotobeat – The operating system for live music

Location: Remote-first (UTC to UTC+3 preferred) | Type: Full-time | Reports to: Head of Tech

Salary: Competitive + equity

How to apply: send your CV to alfredo@gotobeat.com

---

## The problem

Can this artist fill this room, in this city, on this Thursday? Every promoter bets their own money on that question, and most of them answer it with gut feel, a Spotify listener count and a phone call to a friend. A good answer puts the right act in a 300-cap room in Leeds two summers before it headlines a festival. A bad answer leaves a half-empty venue and a lost deposit.

We built a system that answers it better than gut feel. It is called Antonello. We are hiring the person who will own it.

## About Gotobeat

Gotobeat builds software for live music: for the artists who play, the venues that host and the promoters who book. We help emerging artists earn more, venues fill more seats and promoters spend less time on admin. The platform covers planning, promotion, ticketing and post-show settlement. It runs on an AWS serverless stack, Python data pipelines and LLM agents.

## Why this role matters

Most music data companies see one slice: streams, or social, or ticket sales. Gotobeat is a ticketing platform and a promoter tool, so we hold the dataset that ties them together: what an artist streamed, what they posted, where they played and how many people paid at the door. That join is the most valuable thing we own. Today one founder maintains it.

You are the first hire whose whole job is that data. You take over the models, the pipelines and the storage, and you own them end to end: from the notebook where a feature starts to the number a promoter reads before they sign a deal. When your forecast moves, shows get booked or not. The feedback is an empty room or a full one.

## What you take over on day one

* **Antonello, the capacity engine.** A per-city venue-capacity forecast: an XGBoost ensemble over an event-history prior, calibrated ranges, confidence gates that hold back a weak prediction, and an LLM evidence-repair loop that finds the shows our scrapers missed.
* **The discovery loop.** A daily pipeline that pulls new artists from Songstats, Spotify playlists and related-artist graphs, runs them through fit gates, genre families and liveness checks, and gives a promoter a shortlist that matches their taste and their rooms.
* **The data estate.** DynamoDB as the system of record, a change-data-capture mirror into a normalised Postgres schema on Supabase, S3 snapshots, and the API clients and data-partner integrations for streaming, social and touring data.
* **The analytics.** Sell-through and price suggestions, the hype and momentum scores, ad attribution across Meta and Google, and a rule engine that checks the model when the evidence is thin.

## What you'll do

* **35%** Build the best artist model in the music industry. Antonello forecasts what an act can draw in a city. Your job is to make that the number the industry trusts. Retrain it, recalibrate it and score it against what happened at the door. Decide when it should stay silent. Ship each improvement to production yourself.
* **25%** Own the data pipeline and the ingestion. Keep every source complete, fresh and cheap, and make the join between streaming, social, touring and ticket sales something a colleague can query in one line.
* **15%** Own the architecture of the data estate: the single-table design, the change-data-capture mirror into Postgres, and the schema every model and every query reads. Design the contracts so a new source or a new model plugs in without a migration weekend.
* **15%** Build the analytics a promoter bets on: expected sell-through, the right ticket price, which ad spend sold tickets, and the confidence behind each number.
* **10%** Expose the models as tools our LLM agents call, with the evaluation and the guardrails that let an agent draft a deal from a forecast.

## The stack

* Python 3.13 in Lambda containers for the models and the scrapers: XGBoost, numpy, Playwright.
* TypeScript on Node for the orchestration, the API and the promoter product: AWS Lambda, Step Functions, EventBridge, and SST v3 as infrastructure as code.
* DynamoDB with ElectroDB, DynamoDB Streams into Supabase Postgres, S3 for snapshots and artefacts.
* Claude, Gemini and Perplexity for the agents, called through MCP tool surfaces.
* No Kubernetes, no Spark cluster, no GPU farm. The data is small: tens of thousands of artists, hundreds of thousands of shows and the ticket sales behind them.
* No pager. The crons run overnight and the alarms land in Slack.

## You'll be successful here if you have

* Substantial experience of shipping machine learning that people relied on, including at least one model that was wrong in production and what you learned from it.
* Depth in tabular ML and forecasting: gradient boosting, calibration, evaluation on small and noisy data, and a preference for the simpler model that you can explain to a promoter.
* Data engineering: you have designed a schema, owned a pipeline end to end and made an expensive source cheap.
* Fluent Python, and enough TypeScript to ship the glue yourself.
* Practical LLM engineering: tool use, retrieval and evaluation, and a clear view of when a model must ask before it acts.
* Experience of building on your own: from a blank repo to something people use, with nobody else writing the tickets.
* A love of live music. You have stood in a half-empty room and known why.

### Nice to have

* Experience of music or entertainment data, for example at a streaming service, a data provider, a ticketing platform, a label or a booking agency.
* Experience with streaming, social or touring APIs, and with an ingestion that survives an upstream change.
* Experience with AWS serverless data patterns and change-data-capture pipelines.
* Experience with the MCP tool protocol and agent evaluation.

---

## How we work

* Remote-first, with quarterly in-person hack weeks in London.
* A small, senior team with no management layers and a lot of autonomy.
* One-week sprints, async communication and fast decisions.
* The founder who built the current models works with you for the first months, then hands over.
* We value clean code, continuous learning and doing right by artists.

## Benefits

* Competitive salary, set by experience, plus founding-team equity.
* Fully remote, with the hours that suit you.
* We engage you as an employee or as a contractor, according to the country where you live.
* Unlimited paid holiday, plus local public holidays.
* Free gig tickets and backstage passes to all Gotobeat shows.
* A budget for the hardware, the data and the conferences you need.

---

## Hiring process

1. Intro chat (30 min): the role, the music and whether we make sense to each other.
2. Technical deep dive (90 min): you walk us through a model you shipped, then we pair on a prediction from our data that went wrong. No LeetCode, no take-home.
3. Founders' chat (30 min): vision, values, equity and any remaining questions.

Total time from first call to offer: about two weeks.

---

## Ready to join Gotobeat?

Send your CV to alfredo@gotobeat.com with the subject line "Founding ML Engineer – [Your Name]". Tell us about a model you shipped and what it got wrong, and name one artist you think is about to break. We reply within five business days.

Gotobeat is an equal-opportunity employer. We welcome applications from everyone. Tell us if you need any adjustment to the process.

We use your application only to assess you for this role. We keep it for six months after the role closes, then we delete it. See the privacy policy for your rights.

## Job Description

We are looking for a qualified solicitor (England and Wales) with an enthusiasm for competition law, who has 2 – 4 years' experience of working on a range of significant UK and/or EU competition law matters, and is keen to work on high quality instructions within a supportive team environment. 

An EU legal qualification, and/or an interest in trade, customs, and sanctions issues would be useful, but is not essential.

Gowling WLG's award-winning Competition, Foreign Investment & Trade ("**CFIT**") team receives high quality instructions from a diverse client base, and provides clear advice on complex issues.

The CFIT team advises national and international clients on a broad range of areas, including: merger control; NSIA / FDI issues; competition investigations (including dawn raid support); market investigations; the interface between competition law and IP; distribution and licensing arrangements; subsidy control and State aid; and trade, customs, and sanctions. 

In doing so, the team works closely with colleagues across the wider firm and its international offices, including within Gowling WLG's award winning IP, Corporate, and Real Estate teams.

Recent instructions have included:

* Advising Clio on its $1 billion acquisition of vLex.
* Advising Empiric Student Property on its £723 million acquisition by Unite Group, which was notified to, and cleared by, the CMA under the UK merger control regime.
* Advising H&T Group on its $383 million acquisition by FirstCash.
* Advising various clients on FDI issues arising in the context of acquisitions of targets with activities in sectors including advanced materials, AI, energy, and defence, including securing clearances under the NSIA.
* Advising RPSG Group on its acquisition of a majority stake in Manchester Originals.
* Advising a trade association subject to an investigation by the CMA into suspected infringements of UK competition law.
* Advising a manufacturer subject to an investigation by the CMA into suspected infringements of UK competition law, with the European Commission conducting a parallel investigation into suspected infringements of EU competition law.
* Advising businesses on responding to market studies and market investigations in the UK.
* Advising international brands on UK and EU competition law issues arising in the context of distribution arrangements.
* Advising public and private clients on UK subsidy control issues in the context of proposed arrangements.

1. Gradiated is a research lab focused on inference. We co-design software and hardware for efficiently serving open-weight models.
2. Our goal is to maximize intelligence per joule. We work across model behavior, software, systems, and silicon to find better ways to run models.
3. We start by thinking about the model as a mathematical function, and map that out onto hardware and then build software on top of that which is custom to each model. This maximises performance and removes wasted abstractions.
4. We are early. Be the founding content and marketing person in the company.

## Why this role exists

1. Software engineers increasingly rely on models, inference systems, and hardware for almost all of their day-to-day work, but rarely get a clear view of how those systems work. We think they should. Knowledge is power.
2. Our research team produces whitepapers about the inference stack. You will be the translation layer between this work and regular full-stack software engineers who want a deeper understanding of what they are building on top of.

## What you will do

1. Work with our researchers as their work develops, not only after a paper is finished.
2. Turn our whitepapers into articles that teach full-stack engineers the concepts, evidence, and practical consequences of the research.
3. Read new model papers, then explain the architecture, training process, evaluations, strengths, weaknesses, and implications for inference.
4. Build small experiments, benchmarks, diagrams, and code examples when they make an explanation more useful or more honest.

Main Activities

# Logistics Coordinator

Royal Leamington Spa

Ready to revolutionize healthcare, making it faster and more accessible than ever before?

**How we started:**

Founded in 2013 by Dwayne D’Souza, HeliosXwas built on a simple but powerful idea: healthcare should be easier to access, faster to receive, and centred around the individual. From day one, we’ve grown without external funding; scaling profitably through technology, disciplined execution, and deep medical expertise. What started as a challenger idea has become one of the most significant healthcare platforms operating globally today.

**Where we are now:**

We’ve earned the trust of millions of people worldwide through category-leading products and well-known brands, including MedExpress, Dermatica, ZipHealth, RocketRX, and Levity. A key driver of our success is vertical integration; we operate our own manufacturing and proprietary products, led by in-house medical teams, researchers, and pharmacists at the top of their fields.

In 2025, HeliosX treated more than 1.7 million patients globally and reached £781m in revenue, representing +337% year-on-year growth and cementing our position as the clear market leader in the UK. That growth translates into real-world outcomes: our weight-loss treatments helped patients lose 8.5 million kilograms of excess weight in 2025 alone, contributing to an estimated 1,300 fewer cardiac events. This is growth with measurable, life-changing impact at scale.

Today, we operate across four international markets, with successful launches in Germany and Canada and continued expansion in the US. We were also recently recognised in the Sunday Times Top 100 fastest-growing tech companies, further validation of both our momentum and our ambition.

**Where we’re going:**

2026 is another significant year for HeliosX. Our ambition is to surpass £1.1bn in revenue, continue expanding thoughtfully into new international markets and broaden our condition and treatment portfolio. As we scale, we're focused on building the technology, operational excellence and clinical capabilities that will support sustainable long-term growth. Joining HeliosX now means helping shape the systems, teams and products that will define the next chapter of digital healthcare. You'll be solving complex problems at pace, working alongside exceptional people and building products that genuinely improve lives at scale.

**There’s never been a more exciting time to join HeliosX. Come be a part of making our dream of easier and faster healthcare a reality!**

**The Opportunity**

We’re looking for a highly organised and proactive Logistics Coordinator to join our Operations team and play a key role in the day-to-day management of final mile operations across all HeliosX brands and products. This role will work closely with our courier partners to coordinate collections, provide accurate forecasts and ensure deliveries run smoothly, while also supporting performance reporting, investigating delivery failures and managing compensation claims in line with our contractual agreements.

This is a hands-on role in a fast-paced environment, where attention to detail, strong communication and a proactive approach will make a real difference to our operational performance and customer experience.

***This role will be based in our Leamington Spa Hub, with standard working hours of 9:00am–5:00pm, Monday to Friday.***

**What you'll do**

* Reporting and Documentation: Maintain comprehensive records and provide regular reports on inbound and outbound shipments, inventory levels, returns, and overall logistics performance.
* Return Management: Manage the return process from couriers, including handling returns and coordinating with partners, finance, and customer service. Oversee return inventory processes such as disposition and refurbishment.
* Identify inefficiencies in the returns process and develop measures to reduce.
* Collaboration: Build and maintain effective relationships with key stakeholders, including internal teams, partners, and third-party logistics (3PL) partners, to ensure smooth operations and resolve issues as they arise.
* Logistics Optimisation: Identify areas for improvement within logistics and supply chain processes. Collaborate with internal teams and logistics partners to implement enhancements and provide business recommendations for increased efficiency and cost-effectiveness.
* Point of escalation and resolution for day to day service failures
* Plan collections of both inbound collections, Yorkes, pallets and returns. Ensure they are communicated with the Hubs
* Deal with escalations on service - monthly review process in place, using courier data and customer service insights to resolve live issues.
* Delivery success monitoring and tracking, using industry data to assess vs best in class.
* Invoice analysis / sense check - work with finance and fulfilment operations to ensure the correct service types and ship methods are charged and challenged effectively.
* Refund / replacement claims- ensure there is a robust process in place to collect credits for failed deliveries up to our contractual requirements.
* Safety or conduct issues of delivery drivers or couriers investigated and addressed.
* Using couriers data to analyse delivery failures - looking to work with courier partners to improve performance.
* Compare and contrast vs customer service data views on delivery performance.
* Present weekly and monthly performance reports on both service and costs to Supply Chain leadership.
* Work with the product team on courier management system solutions and dashboards.

**What you'll bring to HeliosX**

* 5+ years experience in supply chain operations - specifically within carrier management / or within a courier.
* Proven experience of successful interaction with key stakeholders, both internal and external (third party suppliers).
* Experience within a start up / scale up environment (desirable).
* Pharmacy / healthcare experience advantage but not essential.
* Ability to demonstrate effective cross-functional working to achieve results.
* High level of logical thought used in problem solving.
* Ability to deal with data from various sources and use it to analyse performance and challenge contractors / couriers.
* Good level of excel / Google Sheets competency.
* Experience of working within an ERP or MRP system.
* Good communication written and verbal.
* Comfortable working in a fast paced environment.

**Why work with us?**

At HeliosX, we want to improve healthcare for everyone, and to do this we need a team of brilliant people who share that ambition. We are currently a diverse team of engineers, scientists, clinical researchers, physicians, pharmacists, marketeers, and customer care specialists committed to our mission - but we need more talented folks to join us, if we want to achieve our global ambitions! Aside from working with our all-star team, here are the other benefits of coming on board:

* Annual Leave Allowance
* Private health insurance, along with pre-existing medical conditions, dental and eye care cover
* Pension scheme
* Cycle-to-work Scheme
* Electric Car Scheme
* Free Dermatica and MedExpress products every month, as well as family discounts
* Annual L&D budget
* Access to a Headspace subscription, employee assistance programme and discounted gym memberships

This role carries real weight: your decisions directly shape the customer experience of Helsing and the capabilities we build and deploy. 

## The day-to-day

* Lead end-to-end project management of international field deployments and training courses, ensuring on-time, on-standard delivery across multiple simultaneous engagements globally – from the High-North to the Indo-Asia Pacific and beyond

* Serve as the primary business development lead during customer-facing deployments, building trusted relationships with defence and government stakeholders and feeding structured commercial intelligence back into the wider business

* Deliver HX-2 tactics instruction to customer personnel as the subject-matter expert for the ALTRA recce-strike system, maintaining and evolving course content to reflect the latest operational doctrine and system capabilities

* Act as the senior customer success owner during field engagements, proactively identifying and resolving issues, capturing feedback, and translating customer outcomes into measurable programme, training, and product improvements

* Represent Helsing operationally across international markets, coordinating closely with internal teams (Sales; BD; Production; Logistics; Export Control; Product Management; Legal; and People) to align field activity with strategic business priorities and ensuring a consistent, high-quality customer experience

## You should apply if you

* Have held a leadership position managing complex field operations and/or training programmes in high-stakes, time-critical environments, ideally within a military or defence context

* Have experience in the design, development, and implementation of NATO or equivalent training programmes, including experience of training design frameworks such as: UK DSAT; US SAT / ISD (ADDIE); NATO Systems Approach to Training; and NSIQC

* Are enthused by the prospect of:

* regular overseas deployments with the requirement to operate in field conditions alongside military our partners for 2-3 week periods

* leading and working alongside diverse and exceptionally proficient forward deployed technical engineering colleagues

* training and enabling military users to rapidly develop proficiency on our systems, and to support them beyond initial training on their exercises and operational deployments

* Bring direct, hands-on experience operating or instructing on the HX-2 recce-strike system, or have served as a qualified tactics instructor on a comparable recce-strike, loitering munition UAS platform, or within a support weapon trade such as Javelin anti-tank, reconnaissance, or sniper specialisms

* Have built and sustained trusted relationships with senior defence or government customers, and can credibly operate as a business development lead during live customer engagements

* Hold, or are eligible to obtain, the security clearance required for the operational demands of this role
* Communicate with clarity and authority in English to native standard, with the interpersonal range to operate effectively across diverse international defence audiences

## Join Helsing and work with world-leading experts in their fields

* Helsing’s work is important. You’ll be directly contributing to the protection of democratic countries while balancing both ethical and geopolitical concerns
* The work is unique. We operate in a domain that has highly unusual technical requirements and constraints, and where robustness, safety, and ethical considerations are vital. You will face unique Engineering and AI challenges that make a meaningful impact in the world
* Our work frequently takes us right up to the state of the art in technical innovation, be it reinforcement learning, distributed systems, generative AI, or deployment infrastructure. The defence industry is entering the most exciting phase of the technological development curve. Advances in our field of world are not incremental: Helsing is part of, and often leading, historic leaps forward
* In our domain, success is a matter of order-of-magnitude improvements and novel capabilities. This means we take bets, aim high, and focus on big opportunities. Despite being a relatively young company, Helsing has already been selected for multiple significant government contracts
* We actively encourage healthy, proactive, and diverse debate internally about what we do and how we choose to do it. Teams and individual engineers are trusted (and encouraged) to practise responsible autonomy and critical thinking, and to focus on outcomes, not conformity. At Helsing you will have a say in how we (and you!) work, the opportunity to engage on what does and doesn’t work, and to take ownership of aspects of our culture that you care deeply about

## What we offer

* **Competitive salary** and **VSOP options**
* **Relocation support**: up to €2,500 and 4 weeks temporary accommodation
* **Learning**: €500/£450 yearly allowance
* **Health & wellness**: gym membership and mental health support (Nilo.health)
* **Social**: regular company events and monthly social allowances
* **Enhanced parental leave**: 22 weeks fully paid for primary caregivers & 6 weeks for secondary caregivers
* **Family support:** 5 days of paid family emergency leave, 100% remote work option during pregnancy and phased return to work
* A hands-on onboarding program (affectionately labelled “Infraduction”), in which you will be building tooling and applications to be used across the company. This is your opportunity to learn our tech stack, explore the company, and learn how we get things done - all whilst working with other engineering teams from day one (Specifically for engineering and AI)

*These are the core benefits across all locations, there may be additional benefits in certain locations.*

We’re a small team, which means no part of HR stays out of your reach – payroll, reward, employee relations, regulatory work and people insight all happen close enough to learn from, and there is real room to grow into the areas that interest you most. We learn from each other here, and we will back you to keep building. We’ll also expect you to put AI and automation to work on the routine stuff, because the more effort you take out of the process, the more of the interesting work comes your way.

**KEY RESPONSIBILITIES**

**1. Own the HR mailbox so no colleague is left waiting**

The HR mailbox is the front door to our function, and how quickly and well we respond shapes how the whole business experiences HR. You own it.

* Act as the first point of contact for all HR queries from internal and external stakeholders, resolving routine matters yourself and triaging anything sensitive or requiring judgement to the Senior HR Business Partner.
* Respond to all employee queries within 48 hours – with a full answer where you can, or a clear acknowledgement, owner and expected timescale where you cannot.
* Keep the mailbox organised and current, with nothing sitting unactioned and a clear record of what was asked and answered.
* Track recurring query themes and use them to suggest better guidance, clearer comms or a process fix, so the same question stops arriving.

**2. Own our HRIS as the single source of truth**

You own all administrative processes in our HRIS, The Hive, so that the data in it is complete, current and trusted by HR, Finance, managers and our regulators alike.

* Enter and maintain all employment, pay, work pattern, benefits and documentation records accurately and on time.
* Run periodic data accuracy audits, resolve exceptions and flag the root causes so they stop recurring.
* Maintain the organisation chart monthly and on request.
* Independently produce a range of employee communication, including pay increases, promotions, amended hours, job title changes and study support agreements, and action each change in The Hive.
* Administer family leave – maternity, paternity and shared parental – including entitlement records, documentation, letters and return-to-work changes.
* Keep pace with system updates and new functionality, and support testing of new features.

**3. Deliver an accurate, on-time monthly payroll input every cycle**

* Compile the monthly payroll submission to Finance and maintain the master payroll tracker, keeping it reconciled to The Hive and ready for the payroll sign-off meeting, resolving or escalating any discrepancies.
* Process and log all in-month changes, including approved overtime, referral and one-off bonuses, sickness and fit notes, sick pay entitlement, advance deductions, work pattern and shift changes, promotions and holiday buy/sell.
* Apply the correct statutory and company family leave pay entitlements, and instruct payroll accordingly.
* Produce the monthly benefits reporting pack for our providers.

**4. Deliver a seamless joiner-to-leaver experience**

From first contract to final payslip, you own the administration that shapes how people join us and how they leave.

* Check pre-joining documentation is complete and accurate, draft employment contracts, and manage pre-joining forms, reference requests and manager checklists in The Hive.
* Set new joiners up across all people and benefits systems, check HMRC starter documentation is complete and notify our payroll and benefits providers.
* Confidently deliver the HR induction to small groups of new joiners, and carry out post-induction check-ins.
* Support the probation process, ensuring line managers complete the correct documentation on time and escalating any performance concerns to the Senior HR Business Partner.
* Manage the leaver process end to end – confirmation letters, marking the leaver in The Hive, benefits removal, and calculating holiday balances, clawbacks and outstanding payments for the payroll submission.
* Maintain temporary worker and contractor administration, including contract copies, start, end and extension dates, and inductions.
* Run the new joiner survey and support exit interviews, sharing emerging themes with the wider HR team.

**5. Complete every vetting and SM&CR check to a standard that would stand up to audit**

* Administer the recertification cycle for the certified population, including periodic DBS and credit checks and ongoing right to work and visa tracking.
* Maintain accurate, audit-ready SM&CR records and evidence, chasing colleagues to complete certification requirements on time.

* Prepare clean, reliable datasets for the wider HR team, and provide ad hoc datasets to other functions when required, drawing out insights from the raw data rather than just supplying numbers.
* Produce the attendance tracker every month for all locations, to ensure all employees are in compliance with our attendance policy.
* Respond to routine ad hoc data requests accurately and on time.

This is a high-volume role, and we don’t want you spending your day on work a tool could do. We expect you to actively look for where AI and automation can take effort out of the process, and to use them well and safely - applying your own judgement to every output, and only ever using tools approved for the data you are putting into them.

* Calm and organised under pressure – able to prioritise, multi-task and own a busy recurring calendar of activity without being chased
* Creative and solutions-focused – we are small but complex, and our challenges are genuinely our own, so the textbook answer often will not fit. We are looking for someone who enjoys working out a better way rather than waiting to be told one
* Keen to keep learning – curious about the parts of HR beyond your own remit, and ready to take the opportunities that a small team gives you
* A self-starter who is comfortable assuming responsibility and accountability, and confident tackling things independently – the team will always be there to help, but the pace and variety of the role mean you need to be able to run with things
* Strong written and verbal communication skills, and a confident, friendly manner with people at all levels of the organisation – including the sensitivity to handle personal conversations, such as family leave, with care
* A great team player who is enthusiastic about the impact our team can have

* Graduate, or CIPD Level 5 qualified or above. We are looking for someone who has invested in the professional side of HR, not just picked it up along the way – you should bring a working knowledge of employment practice and the reasoning behind the processes you run, and the appetite to keep building on that qualification with us

Here at Humanoid, we believe in a future where robots amplify human potential. That’s why we’ve set out on a mission to build the world’s most capable, commercially-scalable, and safe humanoid robots. We’re bringing that mission to life with HMND‐01 Alpha - our rapidly developed humanoid platform now running in real industrial pilots - and we’re growing the team to take it even further.

**About the role:**  
At Humanoid, we are working from a simple hypothesis: AI is rapidly transforming engineering. The bottlenecks are shifting from writing code to how efficiently AI-authored changes can be verified.

We’re looking for a Technical Lead to build the platform that lets our engineers move faster with coding agents while protecting our code, infrastructure, and robots. You’ll give developers and agents the environments, context, and tools to work effectively, and build verification and security into the path from task to healthy deployment. This means rethinking how engineering work gets done, not just adding agents to existing processes and establishing the access controls, isolation, and monitoring needed to guard against mistakes, misuse, and new security threats.

This is a hands-on leadership role and the keystone hire for a new team. You’ll build the critical systems yourself, recruit and lead engineers, and work across Developer Tools, Security, Safety, Simulation, and robot software. Success means increasing engineering output while reducing cost and human review per accepted change, without increasing defects or safety risk.  
  
**What you'll do:**

* Own the path from an agent task to a healthy deployed change, including acceptance criteria, execution, verification, merge, rollout, monitoring, and rollback.
* Build secure, reproducible agent runtimes with task-scoped identity, short-lived credentials, bounded access, cost controls, and re-playable execution records. Proactively detect unauthorized agent activity across our compute clusters, whether internal or external.
* Build the interfaces developers use to launch, monitor, and control agents, alongside tooling for agents to collaborate through shared memory, coordinated work, and appropriately authorized access to company resources.
* Reduce the tokens and retries required for accepted work through better context assembly, model and tool routing, caching, task decomposition, and feedback.
* Give agents fast access to builds, tests, simulation, replay, and hardware-in-the-loop, with acceptance criteria they cannot alter.
* Work with engineering teams to make the codebase easier to navigate and verify through clear interfaces, strong invariants, reproducible environments, fast local checks, and well-documented implementation paths.
* Recruit and lead the team while remaining hands-on. Measure success through cost per accepted change, human review time, escaped defects, and time from push to healthy on the robot.

**What we're looking for:**

* Experience building and operating developer tooling or infrastructure used across engineering teams, such as build systems, CI/CD, test infrastructure, deployment pipelines, or internal platforms.
* Strong software engineering skills and comfort working in large codebases or monorepos.
* Practical experience with Linux, containers, and cloud infrastructure, plus working knowledge of Kubernetes
* Hands-on experience using and integrating coding agents into real engineering workflows. You understand how context, tools, and evals affect reliability, latency, and cost, and can talk concretely about what worked and what didn’t.
* Sound security judgment around workload isolation, identity, permissions, and credentials. You can design appropriate boundaries for agents accessing code, infrastructure, and company resources.
* Experience building reliable automated tests or verification systems and diagnosing failures across code, tooling, and infrastructure. You have good judgment about what automated checks establish and where human review still matters.
* Experience leading engineers while remaining hands-on. You can set technical direction, recruit a strong team, and turn an ambitious goal into systems that engineers use and trust.

**What We Offer:**

* Competitive equity: stock options with meaningful upside as we scale.
* 30+ paid days off, including 23 days of annual leave, all UK bank holidays, and additional company closure days (including Christmas–New Year shutdown).
* Private healthcare, including virtual and in-person care.
* Pension scheme with 8% total contribution (5% employee, 3% employer) on full earnings.
* Free daily breakfast, catered lunch, and snacks in-office.
* Work at the frontier - collaborate daily with world-class engineers, researchers, and product experts building the next generation of AI and humanoid robotics.
* Real ownership - direct access to founding leadership, meaningful input on product direction, and the ability to drive key initiatives from day one.

The CTO Office is an independent unit within Product & Customer with a dual mandate: track what is genuinely happening at the frontier of the industry, and convert it into technology strategy and working software inside IFS. It operates close to the executive team, frontier AI labs, robotics OEMs, and strategic partners.

## Job Description

**The role**

You will define and build the robotics integration architecture for the IFS suite and grow the engineering team that delivers it. This is a software role. You will not design actuators, motion control, or perception stacks, and hardware experience is not required. What is required is deep, current working knowledge of the software surfaces of the major robot OEM platforms: their SDKs, APIs, fleet managers, autonomy stacks, data models, and their real limitations.

You will also be the engineering counterpart to our robotics ecosystem: OEMs, robotics foundation model companies, startup networks, and standards bodies. When an OEM partner puts their platform engineers in a room, you are the person on our side of the table.

It is a player-coach role in a unit that ships. You will build the first integrations yourself, prove them with real customers and live demos, then scale the capability through the team you hire.

**What you will do**

* Own the agent-first integration architecture between the IFS suite and robotics OEM platforms, from reference design to production

* Build the abstraction layer that lets IFS agents and applications treat heterogeneous robot fleets as dispatchable, auditable executors of work

* Deliver working integrations hands-on: work order dispatch to robots, mission and task orchestration, telemetry and inspection data flowing into asset and service records

* Evaluate OEM platforms on engineering merit and steer where IFS invests integration effort; kill weak options early

* Represent IFS in technical engagements with robot OEMs, robotics foundation model providers, and interoperability bodies

* Hire and lead a robotics integration engineering team and set its technical bar

* Ship demonstrable outcomes on real customer scenarios and flagship events, on hard dates

* Brief executives and customers on the robotics roadmap in commercial terms

## Qualifications

**What we are looking for**

* 15+ years in software engineering, with several years architecting integration or platform layers used in production at enterprise scale

* Demonstrable working knowledge of at least 2 major robot OEM ecosystems at the SDK and API level: you have built against them, not read about them

* Still keyboard-credible: you prototype, review PRs, and debug integrations. We will verify this in the interview process

* Applied AI capability: production experience with agentic systems, tool use and function calling, and orchestration of long-running autonomous tasks

* Fluency in the operational reality of robots in industrial settings: connectivity, safety interlocks, teleoperation and human-in-the-loop handover, degraded modes, and what actually breaks in deployment

* Experience leading engineering teams and dealing with external partner engineering organisations

* Clear written and spoken communication at executive level; comfortable presenting live demos

**Technical depth expected**

We hire for depth per area, not a keyword count. The named platforms and tools are examples; strong equivalents are fine. Expect to be tested on the areas below.

* OEM platforms and SDKs: hands-on integration experience with platforms such as Boston Dynamics (Spot SDK), Agility Robotics, Unitree, ANYbotics, or comparable quadruped, humanoid, AMR, or drone ecosystems; understanding of their mission APIs, fleet managers, autonomy behaviours, and payload and data interfaces

* Robotics middleware and interoperability: ROS 2 (topics, services, actions, DDS) at integration level; fleet interoperability standards such as VDA 5050, the MassRobotics Interoperability Standard, and Open-RMF; where these standards genuinely work and where they fall short

* Agent-first integration: designing AI agents that plan, dispatch, and supervise robot missions; MCP servers and tool interfaces over robot APIs; orchestration frameworks such as LangGraph, Pydantic AI, or provider-native SDKs; permissioning, human-in-the-loop escalation, and audit trails for autonomous physical action

* Robotics foundation models: working awareness of VLA and omni models for robots (for example SkildAI, Physical Intelligence, Nvidia GR00T) and what they change about the integration surface over the next 2 to 3 years

* Industrial data and telemetry: MQTT, OPC UA, and event-driven ingestion of robot telemetry, inspection imagery, and sensor data into enterprise systems; time-series handling at fleet scale

* Simulation and validation: using simulation environments (Isaac Sim, Gazebo, or OEM-native simulators) to validate integrations and demos without waiting on hardware availability

* Enterprise integration: API design and consumption at scale, including REST, OData, GraphQL, and webhook/event patterns into ERP, EAM, and FSM systems; mapping robot missions onto work orders, assets, and service processes

* Languages and platform: expert-level Python and TypeScript; able to read C++ where OEM SDKs demand it; production Kubernetes and containerisation, CI/CD, and edge deployment patterns for on-site connectivity

* Security and safety posture: identity and authorisation for machine actors, network segmentation for OT environments, and the audit and traceability expectations that come with software commanding physical machines

**What sets candidates apart**

* Prior work connecting robots or autonomous systems to business systems (ERP, EAM, WMS, MES) rather than to other robots

* Exposure to asset-intensive or field service domains: utilities, manufacturing, aviation, energy, logistics

* Experience in an OEM or fleet management vendor engineering organisation, seen from the inside

* Standards body or interoperability consortium participation

* 0-to-1 experience standing up a new engineering capability inside a larger organisation

**How we assess**

A walkthrough of integrations you have personally architected and shipped against real robot platforms, a technical deep dive on your agent-first design approach and how you handle autonomy, safety handover, and auditability, and a working session on a live integration problem. References will be asked specifically about hands-on contribution and OEM engagement, not leadership style.

* International travel to OEM partners, customers, and flagship events (Europe and US, some Asia)

**Role Overview**

The Senior Manager – Corporate FP&A owns cash flow analysis, forecasting, and reporting for the group, and supports the Director – Corporate FP&A across consolidated financial reporting and analysis. This role is responsible for translating complex financial data into clear, actionable insights about cash generation, free cash flow conversion, and group-level P&L movements. The Senior Manager is a trusted financial communicator to senior management and internal stakeholders, helping to ensure consistency of financial narrative and quality of insights.

**Key Responsibilities**

**Cash Flow Analysis & Reporting** - Own group cash flow analysis and reporting as the core focus of the role. Produce the monthly and quarterly cash flow reporting pack, explain movements between forecast, budget, and actuals, and make the drivers of cash generation and cash usage clear to the CFO and senior management. Build the cash bridges that connect P&L performance to cash outcomes.

**Free Cash Flow & Cash Conversion** - Analyse free cash flow and cash conversion across the group, including the working capital drivers behind them—DSO, DPO, unbilled and deferred revenue, collections performance, and the cash profile of the subscription base. Identify where conversion is leaking, quantify the impact, and work with commercial and operational teams to close the gap.

**Cash Forecasting Process & Systems** - Own and continuously improve the group cash forecast model, cadence, and controls. Set the forecasting process across entities and functions, drive accuracy through variance tracking and back-testing, and automate manual steps where the tooling allows. Maintain a single source of truth for the group's cash position and outlook.

**Consolidated Financial Reporting** - Support the Director – Corporate FP&A in coordinating consolidated financial reporting across the organization. Ensure consistency of data, methodology, and narrative across reporting streams. Reconcile variances, validate data quality, and drive continuous improvement in reporting processes and controls.

**Business Driver Analysis & Narrative** - Analyze group-level P&L movements and their cash consequences: why did ARR change? why did gross margin move? what's driving operating leverage or expense growth? and how does each of these land in cash? Articulate the business drivers (volume, pricing, mix, productivity, retention, operational efficiency) in clear, executive-ready narratives. Provide context that helps the Board and CFO understand what's sustainable vs. one-off in financial performance.

**Financial Commentary Development** - Develop monthly/quarterly performance narratives, financial presentations, Board commentary, and forecasting documents, with cash flow and liquidity commentary as a standing component. Coordinate across finance functions to ensure commentary is consistent, fact-based, and highlights the drivers of business performance.

**Liquidity & Financial Planning** - Work with treasury and operations to model the cash and liquidity impact of business decisions. Provide early warning on cash constraints, funding requirements, or opportunities for deployment.

**Ad-Hoc Strategic Analysis** - Support the CEO, CFO, and Strategic Finance team with rapid-turnaround analysis on strategic initiatives, business cases, market conditions, and operational performance. Build financial models that enable scenario planning and decision-making, including the cash implications of each scenario.

May include coordinating with global patient affairs to facilitate regional patient  input into clinical trials. ## **About IRIS**

IRIS Software Group is one of the UK's largest privately held software companies, trusted by 100,000+ businesses, schools and accountancy firms to keep their operations running. Our software pays 1 in 6 UK employees, supports over 12,000 schools, and is relied on by 91 of the top 100 UK accountancy firms.

We're a Great Place to Work® certified employer, recognised for our commitment to well-being, inclusion and development - and we're growing fast.

At IRIS Software Group, we help businesses, schools and organisations work smarter through software. But great software only delivers real value when people understand how to use it confidently.

That’s where IRIS Academy comes in.

IRIS Academy is our online learning platform, helping customers, partners and colleagues build confidence using IRIS software. Through on-demand courses, videos and learning pathways, we help people learn at their own pace, whenever they need support.

As IRIS Academy continues to grow across more of our products, we’re looking for **Content Designers / Digital Learning Designers** to help us create clear, practical and engaging digital learning.

This role would suit someone who has already created learning, training, enablement, instructional or support content, ideally within a software, SaaS, technology or customer education environment.

You don’t need previous experience with IRIS products, but you do need to be confident learning complex software quickly and turning that knowledge into simple, useful learning content.

🧾 **Why This Role Matters**

Every day, thousands of customers rely on IRIS software to run important parts of their organisation. The learning you create will help them understand our products, complete key tasks, solve problems and get more value from the software they use.

Instead of helping one customer at a time, you’ll create content that can support thousands of learners whenever they need it.

📊 **What You'll Be Doing**

You’ll design and build self-paced online learning content for IRIS software products.

This will include turning technical product information, customer workflows and subject matter expertise into structured learning that helps people understand what to do, why it matters and how to do it well.

You’ll work closely with Subject Matter Experts, product specialists and stakeholders across the business to understand products, customer needs and learning outcomes.

You’ll create content such as:

* Online courses and learning pathways
* Clear instructional copy
* Audio or video scripts
* Screenshots, screencasts and short videos
* Knowledge checks, quizzes and assessments
* Supporting learning materials

You’ll also keep content accurate as products change, use learner feedback and data to improve content, and contribute to shared standards across IRIS Academy.

The team is also exploring AI-assisted tools and workflows, so curiosity about new technology and smarter ways of creating content will be important.

🔎 **What We’re Looking For**

We’re looking for someone who can combine clear communication, customer empathy and practical content design skills.

You’ll be a good fit if you have:

* Experience creating digital learning, training, customer education, enablement, instructional or support content.
* Experience explaining software, systems or technical processes in a simple and engaging way.
* Strong written communication skills, with the ability to make complex information clear.
* Experience working with customers, users or internal experts to understand needs and turn them into useful content.
* Confidence asking thoughtful questions, probing for detail and understanding the outcome a learner needs.
* Strong organisation skills and the ability to manage multiple content projects at once.
* Good attention to detail and a focus on accuracy.
* A proactive, curious approach to learning new products and tools.
* Confidence building relationships with stakeholders across different teams.
* A willingness to receive feedback and use it to improve your work.

This role may suit someone from a background in digital learning design, e-learning design, instructional design, customer education, software training, product training, enablement, SaaS customer success, software support, professional services or implementation.

Experience with tools such as Articulate Rise, Camtasia, Learning Management Systems or AI-assisted content creation would be helpful, but is not essential.

🚀 **Why Join Us?**

This is a great opportunity to join a growing team that is shaping how customers learn across IRIS.

You’ll build deep knowledge of our products, work closely with experts across the business, and create learning that has a real impact on customer success.

You’ll also continue developing your own skills in digital learning design, instructional design, video content, authoring tools and AI-assisted content creation.

If you enjoy making complicated things simple, care about helping customers succeed, and want to create learning that supports thousands of people, we’d love to hear from you.

📝 **What Can You Expect From Our Application Process?**

Our process will usually include an online application, an initial conversation with Talent Acquisition, relevant online assessments, and a final interview with the hiring team. The final stage may include a practical role-play or content discussion.

During the process, we’ll want to understand your experience, how you approach learning design, how you work with stakeholders, and how you turn complex information into useful content.

**If you’re curious, customer-focused and enjoy turning complex software into simple learning that helps people succeed, we’d love to hear from you.**

* Leading and developing the Temporary Works function, including the Temporary Works Supervisor and Temporary Works Coordinators.

# Wakehurst Ecological Records Volunteer Wakehurst welcomes over 430,000 visitors per year to explore and enjoy the botanical gardens and wider landscape, managed by Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew. The Landscape & Horticulture Department contains four units: Gardens, Nursery, Arboretum & Conservation and Logistics. Together they provide the horticultural estate management for Wakehurst. The main focus of this voluntary role is to support the above teams with the ongoing development of Wakehurst’s ecological stewardship and monitoring work by capturing and digitalising the many biological surveys and ecological studies that have been carried out over the years. These records include species surveys, habitat assessments, phenology observations, management records, handwritten notebooks, maps, spreadsheets, and monitoring data relating to the Gardens, wider estate, SSSI woodlands, meadows, wetlands, and Loder Valley Nature Reserve. At present, much of this information exists in fragmented and inconsistent formats, making it difficult to synthesise findings, identify long-term ecological trends, or fully use this evidence base to guide stewardship, conservation management, horticultural practice, and future research priorities. This volunteer role would therefore play an important part in helping transform historical knowledge into a coherent and accessible ecological resource.

Apply for this role

Location

Wakehurst, West Sussex

Closing Date

27/09/2026

## Main tasks of the role:

* Digitising and cataloguing historic ecological records, surveys, field notes, species lists, maps, and monitoring data into accessible electronic formats.
* Assisting with the organisation and standardisation of ecological datasets to help create a centralised biological recording archive for Wakehurst.
* Supporting the analysis of long-term ecological trends by comparing historical and contemporary records to identify patterns of species change, habitat condition, phenology shifts, and biodiversity trends over time.
* Helping produce annual summaries and reports which interpret ecological monitoring data and communicate key findings in an accessible and engaging way.
* Assisting with the development graphs, maps, species trend charts, and seasonal records
* Supporting species recording and citizen science initiatives across the site, including opportunities to work alongside specialist recorders, researchers, volunteers, and horticultural teams.
* Helping build a stronger evidence base to inform landscape stewardship, ecological enhancement, climate adaptation, and biodiversity management across the estate.

## **About You:**

* You enjoy working in an office environment, either independently or as part of a small team.
* You are an ecology enthusiast with an eye for detail and an ability to record information accurately and with confidence.
* You feel confident using IT programs.
* You are enthusiastic and interested in the work of Kew / Wakehurst and are committed to this role.

## **What to expect from us:**

* A full induction, basic training and ongoing support and supervision.
* Free entry to Wakehurst and Kew for yourself and an accompanying adult.
* Discounts in Wakehurst and Kew shops and eateries.
* Reimbursement of actual travel expenses incurred up to a set value.
* Wakehurst corporate wear.
* To be treated fairly and with respect.
* To be part of a friendly and dedicated team and volunteering community.
* An opportunity to learn about the amazing biodiversity at Wakehurst, the living plants, the ground-breaking science and other Kew collections.

## **What we expect from you:**

* A willingness to attend basic training/health & safety courses to support operations and give you the knowledge you’ll need to carry out this role (full training will be given in the tasks and use of equipment).
* Ability to navigate the wider landscape using maps.
* Flexibility and willingness to work in inclement weather.
* We suggest a minimum participation of two weekdays a month.
* Able to travel (either by public transport or your own vehicle) to Wakehurst at least two days per month.
* Please note this is a long term role so we welcome applicants that can commit to more than a year.

## **This role will suit volunteers with the following skills and experience:**

 We're looking for a Data Analyst who can turn raw operational, payments, and enrollment data into a clear picture of where fraud risk is emerging across our programs, translate those patterns into recommendations that change how projects are designed, and partner with our Product team to build the tools that help us catch fraud earlier and more reliably. job_description: Klarna, briefly At Klarna, we're building an everyday finance network, helping over 120 million consumers across 26 countries save time and money, and worry less about their finances. Working here means taking on problems most companies never get to solve, and being hands-on enough that the interesting part of the work lands with you, not someone else — you'll build with AI, not watch it happen. This is the stretch zone. Come find out what you're capable of. About the role First-line fraud teams at Klarna build models against real-time attacks on payments, logins, and identity — trained on transaction volumes north of 100 million records and pipelines with hundreds of features. Your job is to make sure those models actually hold up: independently reproducing results, building challenger models, and stress-testing every assumption from data pipeline to production deployment before a model earns trust at scale. This is a second-line position, reviewing methodologies built with scikit-learn, LightGBM, graph models, anomaly detection, and increasingly GenAI-based components. You'll also build your own tooling — agentic AI systems that read model documentation and code and surface risks automatically, so validation keeps pace with how fast first-line teams ship. The scope spans the full model lifecycle: data integrity and feature engineering, conceptual soundness, deployment design across Docker, Jenkins, and AWS, and the monitoring and drift detection that keeps a model honest after launch. What you'll do You'll assess model performance using fraud-specific metrics — precision/recall, ROC-AUC, PR-AUC, cost-sensitive metrics, and fraud capture rate — and weigh each against its real business trade-off. You'll review transaction datasets exceeding 100 million records and feature pipelines with hundreds of features for representativeness, leakage risk, and bias. You'll evaluate drift detection, retraining strategies, and production monitoring practices to confirm they catch degradation before it costs the business. You'll assess CI/CD and deployment controls — Docker, Jenkins, and the AWS SageMaker, S3, Athena, and Lambda environments models run in. You'll evaluate model governance documentation, explainability approaches, and compliance with regulatory expectations on model risk, fairness, and data privacy. You'll validate emerging techniques as first-line teams adopt them — graph networks, behavioral biometrics, anomaly detection, and GenAI-based systems. You'll document validation outcomes and communicate model risks directly to first-line data scientists, ML engineers, and business stakeholders. Who you are You've spent 3+ years hands-on in fraud-related modeling — transaction fraud, account takeover, identity fraud, or payments fraud. You know tree-based models like LightGBM, anomaly detection techniques, and graph or network models well enough to challenge someone else's implementation choices, not just build your own. You've worked across the full ML lifecycle — from feature engineering through production deployment and monitoring — and know where each stage tends to go wrong. You're fluent in Python and SQL, and you've used PySpark or Spark to process data at scale. You've built agentic AI workflows — not just used off-the-shelf tools, but designed the automation yourself. You understand model validation principles and model risk governance well enough to assess bias, fairness, explainability, and privacy risk, not just accuracy. You can take a complex model apart, explain what's wrong with it, and make that case clearly to both technical teams and senior stakeholders who aren't. Bonus points for An advanced degree (Master's or PhD) in a quantitative field such as data science, statistics, mathematics, computer science, physics, or engineering. Experience in BNPL, credit cards, or other transaction-heavy payment products. You've mentored junior validators or led validation reviews. Exposure to inference on rejected transactions and how fraud risk and credit risk overlap. Familiarity with AI governance frameworks and emerging AI regulatory requirements. Things you should know before applying Working together: we value co-located teams; most teams currently meet in the office 2–3 days per week, and this varies by team and can change over time. Non-obvious backgrounds are welcome. Diversity of skills, perspectives, and backgrounds is how we create, innovate, and disrupt like no other. Final compensation will be based on the candidate's qualifications, skills, and experience. This is a second-line, independent validation position — you'll work closely with first-line fraud data science and ML engineering teams, without reporting into them. Please include a CV in English. Concrete beats comprehensive — what you built, what it did, what it cost. Curious to learn more about Klarna and what it's like to work here? Explore our career site!

## Description

Landytech is on a mission to revolutionise the way that investment managers, asset owners and their advisors access asset information. Powered by Sesame, an industry-leading investment reporting platform, we are helping clients in over 15 countries make informed investment decisions and deliver insights faster.

The company is growing rapidly and it's an exciting time to join, having secured $12M in Series B funding in January 2023. In just four years, it has gone from two co-founders to a team of 80+ staff, with offices in London and Paris. At Landytech, we see diversity as our strength with a team from over 15 countries and 14 languages spoken.

**The role**

AI has made producing screens easy. It has not made products coherent. We are looking for someone to own the experience of Sesame end to end - the client journey, the interaction logic, the look and feel, and the consistency of all of it.

*We have posted this role under two titles - Product Experience Designer and Design Engineer - to reach both backgrounds. Same role, same team. Apply once, to whichever fits you better.*

**How we work**

We have rebuilt our product process around AI rather than bolting it on:

* AI is used heavily at every stage of both design and engineering, not just at the production end
* Our design system lives in code, used by engineers and AI tooling alike
* Tooling changes every few months and we expect it to
* You will have real scope to shape how we work, and to help build the parts that do not exist yet.

**What you will shape**

How much of this you lead outright will depend on your experience and on how it fits with the team already in place. There is room to take on more over time.

* **Client journey.** The journey for investment professionals, family offices and their advisors - grounded in time spent with them, not personas
* T**he experience model.** How portfolios, positions, transactions and valuations are represented, related and navigated across the platform - and a strong voice when teams disagree
* **Look, feel and consistency.** The product should feel like one thing, and you will help define what that one thing is
* **The design system.** A living implementation in code, developed with our front-end engineers rather than a Figma library that drifts from production
* **Craft in dense financial interfaces.** Tables that stay legible at scale, numbers at the right precision, drill-downs that survive a messy real portfolio

**The must-have: setting the standard AI works to**

AI is very good at producing attractive interfaces. Given a design system, almost anyone can now generate a credible screen.

The harder problem, and the one this role exists to solve, is making sure what we build expresses the product's logic, density and intent rather than simply reusing its components. That means defining the standards and instructions our tools work to, reading the output critically enough to see why something is subtly wrong, and tightening the rules so it does not recur.

Using AI to produce interfaces is not the skill we are looking for. Directing it to our standard, consistently and at depth, is.

**Strongly valued: front-end engineering experience**

Designing the experience is half of it. Delivering it is the other half.

* Build and ship, rather than only specify
* Drive the design system with engineers as a shared artefact in code
* Design for real production constraints: scale, loading and error states, ugly data

You do not need to be a full-time engineer. Comfort reading a component, working in a library such as shadcn/ui and reviewing a front-end PR goes a long way.

**Also valued: product management instincts**

If you have talked to clients directly, decided what not to build, and owned an outcome rather than a deliverable, we will weight it heavily.

**What we are looking for**

We do not expect anyone to have everything below - we would rather meet someone exceptional in two areas than adequate in all three.

* 5+ years designing B2B, analytics or data-heavy products, with deep UX expertise in complex domains
* Systems thinking - you think in objects, relationships and states before screens
* Real craft in dense data interfaces: tables, grids, charts, hierarchy, typography, restraint
* Fluency with AI-assisted design as a working method, and the specification skill described above
* First-hand user research - you get past what users say they do to what they actually do
* Comfortable as an editor and enabler: reviewing others' work, teaching, holding a line
* Genuine curiosity about finance. You need not arrive knowing what a capital call is

**Our process**

Our interview process is likely to include a portfolio or work conversation, a short practical exercise based on a real Sesame flow, and a working session with a product manager and an engineer. We adapt the steps to the candidate and will always tell you what to expect in advance.

* Hybrid working
* Private medical insurance with Bupa for you and your family
* Death in service insurance option
* Pension plan with NEST
* Cycle to Work scheme and gym allowance
* Office food and drinks, regular socials

Powered by talent and advanced technology, our single and multi-manager investment strategies are underpinned by deep research and span public and private markets, across all major asset classes, with a significant focus on alternatives. Headquartered in London, we manage $253.6 billion* and operate across multiple offices globally. Man Group plc is listed on the London Stock Exchange under the ticker EMG.LN and is a constituent of the FTSE 250 Index. Further information can be found www.man.com
At Man Group, we respect your privacy and we are committed to protecting and safeguarding your Personal Data. The Role
As a Quant Developer at Man Group you will be part of one of our flagship teams in Man’s systematic trading arm - Man AHL. The team works hand-in-hand with Quant Researchers focusing on equity market neutral models. Your challenges will be varied, and will involve building new alphas and new trading strategies.
The Team
Quant Developers at Man Group are all part of our broader technology team, members of a group of over sixty individuals representing eighteen nationalities. We have varied backgrounds including Computer Science, Mathematics, Physics, Engineering – even Classics - but what unifies us is a passion for technology and writing high-quality code.
Our developers are organised into small cross-functional teams, with our engineering roles broadly of two kinds: “Quant Platform Developers” otherwise known as our “Core Techs”, and “Quant Developers” which we often refer to as “Sector Techs”. We use the term “Sector Tech” because some of our teams are aligned with a particular asset class or market sector. Our Technology
Our systems are almost all running on Linux and most of our code is in Python, with the full scientific stack: numpy, scipy, pandas, scikit-learn to name a few of the open-source libraries we use extensively. We implement the systems that require the highest data throughput in Java and C++.
We use Airflow for workflow management, Kafka for data pipelines, Bitbucket for source control, Jenkins for continuous integration, Grafana + Prometheus for metrics collection, ELK for log shipping and monitoring, Docker and Kubernetes for containerisation, OpenStack for our private cloud, Ansible and Terraform for architecture automation, and Slack for internal communication. We heavily utilise ArcticDB (https://arcticdb.io/) our in-house developed DataFrame Database. Technology and Business Skills
At AHL we strive to hire only the brightest and best and most highly skilled and passionate technologists.
Essential
Exceptional technology skills; recognised by your peers as an expert in your domain

**About Marex**

Marex Group plc (NASDAQ: MRX) is a diversified global financial services platform providing essential liquidity, market access and infrastructure services to clients across energy, commodities and financial markets.

The group provides comprehensive breadth and depth of coverage across four core services: clearing, agency and execution, market making, and hedging and investment solutions. It has a leading franchise in many major metals, energy and agricultural products, with access to 60 exchanges. The group provides access to the world’s major commodity markets, covering a broad range of clients that include some of the largest commodity producers, consumers and traders, banks, hedge funds and asset managers. With more than 40 offices worldwide, the group has over 3,000 employees across Europe, Asia and the Americas.

For more information visit https://www.marex.com/

**Role Summary**

Develop centralised core datasets for Marex’s trading systems, globally across the firm, to the standards of a listed environment for purposes such as:

* Enterprise level dataset integration
* Management P&L reporting
* Balance Sheet Substantiation
* Statutory Reporting

Build an extensive knowledge of Marex’s business operations, covering booking models, source systems and data flows, to work towards the systematic development of the required data sets.

Build tools that make use of these datasets, for example:

* Reconciling them to the general ledger
* Using them to automate parts of Finance’s workload
* Exposing them to AI tools

Partner with the enterprise data engineers, and data analytics teams working towards the target state solution for sourcing and reporting data for the firm. Become SME for these datasets and tools, document them and ensure smooth adoption by Finance and robust integration into enterprise datasets to describe the firm in granular and timely terms.

**Responsibilities**

* Work with internal teams to develop core datasets for the various trading systems in use at Marex.  Refine these datasets to ensure they meet Finance’s requirements for management P&L reporting, balance sheet substantiation, statutory reporting including ensuring they can be effectively interpreted by AI tools.
* Build reconciliations and similar to ensure these datasets tie to the general ledger *and*
  to assist Finance in using them for the abovementioned tasks.  Typically, the build will take place using End User Computing (“*EUC*”) applications such as Alteryx.
* Partner with the enterprise data engineers and analytics teams to validate integrated datasets against the general ledger and act as the liaison and representative for Finance into enterprise level dataset creation and maintenance across the wider firm.
* Work with IT department to manage any parts of the build not being implemented through EUCs.
* Design and execute UAT testing for all tools built and any subsequent changes.
* Become subject matter expert on these datasets and associated tools.  Document the datasets and tools and provide training to the wider Finance team to ensure effective adoption.
* Crosstrain others within the Finance Change team on the tools built to ensure coverage.
* Longer term, work with the IT department to migrate these tools onto IT-owned platforms.

**Skills and Experience:**  
*Required*

* Extensive experience working in Finance in a regulated environment, and knowledge of the risk and compliance requirements associated with this
* Exceptional problem solving skills
* Control-focused and detail-oriented mind-set
* Demonstrable interest in data-manipulation techniques
* Highly advanced, up-to-date knowledge of Microsoft Excel

*Beneficial*

**Key responsibilities**

•  Lead the design, build, test, deployment and support of solutions using Power Apps, Power Automate, Dataverse, Copilot Studio and appropriate pro-code extensions.

•  Engineer AI agents and agentic workflows using trusted knowledge, tools, actions, approvals, human hand-offs, evaluation and safe failure paths.

•  Design and implement integrations with approved MCP servers and lead development of MCP tools or services using secure, reusable patterns.

•  Integrate Power Platform and AI solutions with Microsoft 365, SharePoint, Microsoft Graph, Azure services and enterprise systems using connectors, APIs and event-based patterns.

•  Apply grounding, retrieval-augmented generation, structured outputs, tool calling and model-selection patterns with appropriate evaluation and operational controls.

•  Create custom connectors, plug-ins and Azure-hosted components where low-code capability is insufficient, choosing technologies based on need, risk and supportability.

•  Set and apply engineering standards for source control, solution packaging, environment strategy, automated testing, CI/CD, monitoring and release management.

•  Review designs and code, mentor developers and contribute reusable components, patterns and learning to the wider engineering community.

## About Millbank FX

Millbank FX is a London-based foreign exchange and global payments specialist, trusted by mid-market and enterprise businesses to manage currency risk and international payments with speed, precision, and integrity.
